Advantages of CNC Technology Applications of CNC Technology in Manufacturing CNC Machine Technology Industrial CNC Technology CNC Technology Services Future Trends in CNC Technology Conclusion CNC technology plays a strategic role in modern manufacturing ecosystems by enabling scalable, automated, and data-driven production across multiple industries. Rather than focusing on individual machines, CNC technology connects digital design, machining processes, and quality systems into an integrated manufacturing workflow. This allows manufacturers to achieve higher throughput, tighter tolerances, and more predictable production outcomes across the entire product lifecycle. By integrating digital design files with computer-controlled machinery, CNC systems allow manufacturers to produce complex parts with consistent accuracy, scalability, and efficiency. From prototyping to full-scale industrial production, CNC technology supports faster workflows, tighter tolerances, and seamless coordination between design, machining, and quality control. For readers who want a clear definition of CNC and a foundational explanation of how CNC machines operate, we provide a dedicated CNC meaning and definition guide that focuses specifically on terminology and basic concepts. To translate CNC technology into real manufacturing outcomes, professional machining services play a critical role. JLCCNC provides CNC machining solutions that support prototyping, small-batch production, and industrial-scale manufacturing, enabling companies to apply CNC technology efficiently without investing in in-house capacity. What is CNC Technology? CNC technology refers to the integrated use of software, control systems, and automated machinery to manage and execute precision manufacturing processes. In modern production environments, CNC technology functions as a core manufacturing platform—linking digital design data with machining operations, tool management, and quality control systems. Advantages of CNC Technology CNC technology offers a wide range of advantages that make it essential to modern manufacturing. By combining computer-controlled automation with high-performance machinery, CNC systems significantly improve manufacturing efficiency. They also enable superior quality and scalability across diverse industries. High Precision and Consistent Accuracy One of the most significant advantages of CNC technology is its ability to deliver extremely high precision. CNC technology can repeatedly produce components with tight tolerances that are difficult or impossible to achieve through manual machining. Once a program is validated, the same dimensions and surface quality can be maintained across thousands of parts, ensuring consistent accuracy even in complex geometries. This level of precision is especially critical in industries such as aerospace, automotive, medical devices, and electronics, where small dimensional deviations can affect performance, safety, or compliance with industry standards. Increased Production Efficiency CNC technology dramatically improves production efficiency by automating machining operations. Machines can run continuously with minimal operator intervention, reducing setup time and accelerating production cycles. Multi-axis CNC systems further enhance efficiency by completing multiple operations—such as milling, drilling, and contouring—in a single setup. Automated tool changes, optimized tool paths, and high-speed machining capabilities allow manufacturers to shorten lead times and respond quickly to changing production demands. Excellent Repeatability and Quality Control Repeatability is a core strength of CNC technology. Every part produced from the same CNC program is virtually identical, minimizing variation and reducing scrap rates. This repeatability simplifies quality control processes, as fewer manual inspections are required once a process is stabilized. CNC systems also integrate easily with in-process measurement and inspection technologies, enabling real-time quality monitoring and early detection of deviations before defects occur. Material and Design Versatility CNC technology supports a wide range of materials, including metals, plastics, composites, and engineered alloys. From aluminum and stainless steel to advanced polymers and titanium, CNC machines can be optimized to handle different cutting characteristics and surface finish requirements. A common example is aluminum CNC machining , which is widely used due to aluminum’s excellent machinability and strength-to-weight ratio. In addition, CNC technology enables the machining of complex shapes, internal features, and intricate contours that would be extremely time-consuming or impractical with conventional methods. This design freedom allows engineers to innovate without being limited by manufacturing constraints. Scalability from Prototyping to Mass Production Another key advantage of CNC technology is its scalability. The same CNC setup can be used for rapid prototyping, small-batch production, and high-volume manufacturing with minimal modification. Design changes can be implemented quickly by updating the digital program rather than retooling entire production lines. This flexibility is particularly valuable for startups, R&D teams, and manufacturers operating in fast-moving markets where product iterations are frequent. Reduced Labor Dependency and Improved Safety By automating machining tasks, CNC technology reduces reliance on manual labor and lowers the risk of human error. Operators are less exposed to cutting tools and moving machine components, resulting in a safer working environment. Modern CNC systems also feature built-in safety controls, error detection, and machine monitoring functions that further protect both personnel and equipment while maintaining stable production. Cost Efficiency Over the Product Lifecycle While CNC machines require an initial investment, they offer long-term cost advantages. Reduced material waste, lower rework rates, shorter production times, and improved machine utilization all contribute to a lower cost per part over the product lifecycle. For manufacturers seeking consistent quality, predictable output, and efficient resource usage, CNC technology represents a cost-effective solution that supports sustainable growth. Applications of CNC Technology in Manufacturing CNC technology has a wide range of applications across industries due to its ability to deliver high precision, consistency, and production efficiency. From large-scale industrial manufacturing to rapid prototyping, CNC technology continues to expand as materials, software, and machine capabilities evolve. Applications in Metalworking CNC milling machines, lathes, and laser cutters handle metals like aluminum, steel, and titanium with unmatched precision. These machines reduce manual labor, minimize errors, and allow for complex shapes that meet rigorous industry standards. In metalworking industries where tolerance control and material consistency are critical, CNC technology enables reliable production of complex metal components at scale. Applications in Plastics and Woodworking Beyond metals, CNC routers can cut, engrave, and shape plastic components or wood panels with high accuracy. Routers are typically used for wood and plastic materials, while milling machines are better suited for metal machining due to their rigidity and cutting capabilities. Manufacturers can efficiently produce prototypes and mass-produced items, lowering production costs and turnaround times. Industrial Applications Industries such as automotive, aerospace, electronics, energy, and heavy machinery rely on CNC systems to produce structural components, housings, brackets, and precision parts. CNC machining ensures tight tolerances, repeatability, and high reliability for critical components. Prototyping and Small Batch Production Rapid prototyping and small-batch CNC production allow engineers to quickly transform digital designs into functional prototypes, enabling faster design validation, iterative testing, and reduced time-to-market. Innovative Uses in Various Industries Advanced applications such as multi-axis cutting, hybrid additive-subtractive manufacturing, and complex 3D contour machining expand possibilities in medical devices, architecture, and custom design. CNC Machine Technology Types of CNC Machines CNC machine technology includes milling machines, lathes, routers, plasma cutters, and laser engraving systems. Each type serves a specific function, from cutting and drilling to shaping and engraving, meeting diverse manufacturing needs. How CNC Machines Work CNC machines operate by translating digital designs into precise machining actions through integrated control systems. This enables highly accurate and repeatable production while minimizing material waste and optimizing workflow efficiency. Maintenance and Optimization Proper maintenance of CNC machines is essential for long-term performance. Regular calibration, tool replacement, and software updates optimize machine efficiency and prevent downtime. Skilled operators can further enhance productivity by choosing the right tooling and machining parameters. Industrial CNC Technology Automation in Large-Scale Production Industrial CNC technology enables full automation of production lines. Large-scale manufacturing can run continuously with minimal human supervision, improving throughput and reducing labor costs. Integration with Industrial Processes CNC technology integrates seamlessly with industrial processes such as assembly, quality inspection, and material handling. This integration allows for smarter factories, streamlined workflows, and higher overall efficiency. Case Studies Industries adopting industrial CNC technology have reported reduced production errors, faster turnaround times, and improved product consistency. For example, automotive suppliers use CNC machines to produce engine components with precise tolerances, enhancing vehicle performance and reliability. CNC Technology Services Design and Consulting Services CNC technology services extend beyond machining itself. Design and consulting services help manufacturers apply CNC technology effectively by optimizing material selection, machining strategies, and process planning before production begins. Manufacturing and Prototyping Services Service providers offer CNC machining for both prototypes and mass production. This allows businesses to outsource specialized tasks, reduce overhead, and maintain high-quality standards. Maintenance and Support Services Many CNC technology service providers also offer ongoing maintenance, troubleshooting, and training. This ensures clients can maintain efficient operations, extend machine lifespan, and minimize production delays. Future Trends in CNC Technology Beyond basic CNC operation and machine control, future CNC technology development is increasingly driven by intelligence, connectivity, and system-level integration. Future developments will not only improve precision and productivity but also fundamentally reshape how factories operate, how products are designed, and how manufacturers compete in global markets. Smart CNC and AI Integration The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with CNC systems is transforming machining from reactive automation into predictive and adaptive manufacturing. AI-powered algorithms can analyze historical machining data. They automatically optimize tool paths, reduce cycle times, and minimize tool wear. Machine learning models are increasingly used to detect subtle signs of tool degradation or misalignment before they cause defects. In aerospace and medical device manufacturing, where tolerances are extremely tight, AI-assisted CNC tool path optimization is already being adopted to ensure consistency and precision across complex geometries. Over time, smart CNC machines will be able to adjust cutting strategies in real time, self-correcting for material inconsistencies and dynamic load variations without human intervention. IoT and Connected Manufacturing The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) enables CNC machines to become integral components of connected smart factories. Sensors embedded in CNC equipment collect real-time data on temperature, vibration, spindle load, and tool life. This data, streamed through secure networks, feeds into centralized manufacturing execution systems (MES) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems to support real-time monitoring and informed decision-making. Connected CNC machines can automatically schedule maintenance based on actual usage patterns, reducing unplanned downtime. In facilities with multiple machines producing different parts, IoT connectivity enhances workflow coordination, material tracking, and quality control, leading to higher operational efficiency and lower production costs. Advanced Materials and Machining Techniques As new materials continue to emerge, CNC technology evolves to address the challenges they present. Advanced composites, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) , and next-generation polymers have unique machining requirements. High-entropy alloys are composed of multiple principal elements in near-equal proportions, offering exceptional strength, wear resistance, and thermal stability. These materials are increasingly used in aerospace and energy applications, where CNC machining must precisely control cutting forces and heat generation to maintain part integrity. CNC technology is also incorporating hybrid manufacturing techniques that combine additive manufacturing (3D printing) with traditional subtractive machining. These hybrid processes allow complex internal structures to be built additively and then finished with high-precision CNC cutting, making them ideal for lightweight aerospace components and customized medical implants. Human–Machine Collaboration and Augmented Reality Future CNC environments will emphasize human–machine collaboration, where operators work alongside intelligent machining systems rather than simply monitoring them. Augmented reality (AR) tools will support setup, training, and maintenance by overlaying digital instructions directly onto physical machinery. Technicians wearing AR headsets will be guided step-by-step through complex calibration or repair processes, reducing training time and lowering the risk of error. Furthermore, virtual simulation environments will allow engineers to preview machining operations before any material is cut. This not only helps validate designs but also ensures that tooling and fixturing are optimized for efficiency and safety. Conclusion Summary of Key Benefits CNC technology has transformed modern manufacturing by improving precision, efficiency, and flexibility. It enables complex machining, reduces errors, and accelerates production cycles. Impact on Modern Manufacturing With industrial CNC technology, advanced machines, and comprehensive services, manufacturers can achieve high-quality output, innovate rapidly, and maintain a competitive edge. As CNC technology continues to evolve, its influence on the manufacturing industry will only grow stronger. Skilled operators can further enhance productivity by choosing the right tooling and machining parameters. Industrial CNC Technology Automation in Large-Scale Production Industrial CNC technology enables full automation of production lines. Large-scale manufacturing can run continuously with minimal human supervision, improving throughput and reducing labor costs. Integration with Industrial Processes CNC technology integrates seamlessly with industrial processes such as assembly, quality inspection, and material handling. This integration allows for smarter factories, streamlined workflows, and higher overall efficiency. Case Studies Industries adopting industrial CNC technology have reported reduced production errors, faster turnaround times, and improved product consistency. For example, automotive suppliers use CNC machines to produce engine components with precise tolerances, enhancing vehicle performance and reliability. CNC Technology Services Design and Consulting Services CNC technology services extend beyond machining itself. Design and consulting services help manufacturers apply CNC technology effectively by optimizing material selection, machining strategies, and process planning before production begins. Manufacturing and Prototyping Services Service providers offer CNC machining for both prototypes and mass production. This allows businesses to outsource specialized tasks, reduce overhead, and maintain high-quality standards. Maintenance and Support Services Many CNC technology service providers also offer ongoing maintenance, troubleshooting, and training. This ensures clients can maintain efficient operations, extend machine lifespan, and minimize production delays. Future Trends in CNC Technology Beyond basic CNC operation and machine control, future CNC technology development is increasingly driven by intelligence, connectivity, and system-level integration. Future developments will not only improve precision and productivity but also fundamentally reshape how factories operate, how products are designed, and how manufacturers compete in global markets. Smart CNC and AI Integration The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with CNC systems is transforming machining from reactive automation into predictive and adaptive manufacturing. AI-powered algorithms can analyze historical machining data. They automatically optimize tool paths, reduce cycle times, and minimize tool wear. Machine learning models are increasingly used to detect subtle signs of tool degradation or misalignment before they cause defects. In aerospace and medical device manufacturing, where tolerances are extremely tight, AI-assisted CNC tool path optimization is already being adopted to ensure consistency and precision across complex geometries. Over time, smart CNC machines will be able to adjust cutting strategies in real time, self-correcting for material inconsistencies and dynamic load variations without human intervention. IoT and Connected Manufacturing The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) enables CNC machines to become integral components of connected smart factories. Sensors embedded in CNC equipment collect real-time data on temperature, vibration, spindle load, and tool life. This data, streamed through secure networks, feeds into centralized manufacturing execution systems (MES) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems to support real-time monitoring and informed decision-making. Connected CNC machines can automatically schedule maintenance based on actual usage patterns, reducing unplanned downtime. In facilities with multiple machines producing different parts, IoT connectivity enhances workflow coordination, material tracking, and quality control, leading to higher operational efficiency and lower production costs. Advanced Materials and Machining Techniques As new materials continue to emerge, CNC technology evolves to address the challenges they present. Advanced composites, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) , and next-generation polymers have unique machining requirements. High-entropy alloys are composed of multiple principal elements in near-equal proportions, offering exceptional strength, wear resistance, and thermal stability. These materials are increasingly used in aerospace and energy applications, where CNC machining must precisely control cutting forces and heat generation to maintain part integrity. CNC technology is also incorporating hybrid manufacturing techniques that combine additive manufacturing (3D printing) with traditional subtractive machining. These hybrid processes allow complex internal structures to be built additively and then finished with high-precision CNC cutting, making them ideal for lightweight aerospace components and customized medical implants. Human–Machine Collaboration and Augmented Reality Future CNC environments will emphasize human–machine collaboration, where operators work alongside intelligent machining systems rather than simply monitoring them. Augmented reality (AR) tools will support setup, training, and maintenance by overlaying digital instructions directly onto physical machinery. Technicians wearing AR headsets will be guided step-by-step through complex calibration or repair processes, reducing training time and lowering the risk of error. Furthermore, virtual simulation environments will allow engineers to preview machining operations before any material is cut. This not only helps validate designs but also ensures that tooling and fixturing are optimized for efficiency and safety. Conclusion Summary of Key Benefits CNC technology has transformed modern manufacturing by improving precision, efficiency, and flexibility. It enables complex machining, reduces errors, and accelerates production cycles. Impact on Modern Manufacturing With industrial CNC technology, advanced machines, and comprehensive services, manufacturers can achieve high-quality output, innovate rapidly, and maintain a competitive edge. As CNC technology continues to evolve, its influence on the manufacturing industry will only grow stronger. Applications of CNC Routing The Real Reasons CNC Routing Dominates FAQ (Istock) (A CNC router cutting into wood) What Is CNC Routing? When people ask what is CNC routing , they're usually trying to figure out one thing: how machines can carve clean shapes out of wood, plastic, and soft metals without human hands guiding the cut every second. CNC routing is essentially a computer-driven cutting system. It uses a tool that spins fast, really fast, to remove material following a pre-programmed path. The machine handles the motion autonomously, without human intervention, following precise digital instructions. This guarantees shops can produce identical components over and over. This makes them ideal for work with high-volume<dynamic-value> decorative panels. So, what is CNC routing in plain terms? It's just automated carving, on a massive scale. A router bit spins, moves across a flat sheet of material, and then cuts shapes, grooves, holes, and contours exactly as designed in the CAD file. The entire process, the depth, the speed, the path, is controlled by motors and software. Unlike a manual hand router, this system works directly from a digital file. This makes every single pass predictable, consistent, and fully repeatable, even if you run hundreds of parts. Routing vs. Other Methods You need to know that routing isn't like laser cutting, plasma, or traditional milling. Lasers burn. Plasma melts. Milling involves much higher forces for deep metal cuts. CNC routing is optimized for large sheets and softer materials. It absolutely excels at cutting MDF, wood panels, PVC foam, acrylic , aluminum composites, and various plastics, cleanly, and very fast. The cutting forces are low compared to milling, making it perfect for flatbed production. Understanding what is CNC routing clarifies why it's the dominant method for things like cabinetry and sign-making. You see CNC routing everywhere in actual production shops: Furniture panels and cabinet doors. Custom engraved lettering and large signs. Acrylic point-of-sale displays. Foam inserts for packaging. Light sheet components made of aluminum. Any time you need clean, repeatable cuts on sheet material, routing is almost always the fastest, most cost-effective method available. How CNC Routing Works CNC routing works by following a precise, computer-generated toolpath to remove material from a workpiece. The process starts with a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) file , which defines the shape, dimensions, and features of the part. This CAD design is then imported into CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing) software , where toolpaths, cutting speeds, spindle speeds, and depths of cut are calculated. Once the program is ready, it is sent to the CNC router. The router uses servo-controlled motors to move the cutting tool along multiple axes—typically X, Y, and Z for standard 3-axis machines, with additional rotary axes for more complex 4- or 5-axis setups. The spinning router bit removes material according to the programmed path, producing precise cuts, grooves, and contours without the need for manual intervention. Key steps in the CNC routing process include: Material Setup – Secure the workpiece on the router bed using clamps or vacuum tables to prevent movement during cutting. Tool Selection – Choose the appropriate router bit for the material and type of cut, considering diameter, flute type, and coating. Spindle and Feed Settings – Adjust spindle speed, feed rate, and depth per pass based on material type, thickness, and bit geometry. Test Cuts – Run a small test cut to verify toolpath accuracy, edge quality, and material behavior before full production. Full Production Run – Execute the complete toolpath with continuous monitoring of material removal, chip evacuation, and machine stability. CNC routing allows for high repeatability, consistent surface finish, and complex geometries across a wide range of materials. Unlike manual routing, it eliminates human error, fatigue, and variability, making it ideal for large-format panels, decorative elements, signage, and prototyping . By understanding how CNC routing works, operators can optimize toolpaths, reduce cycle times, extend tool life, and achieve high-quality results with minimal material waste. Types of CNC Routing Machines Multiple CNC routing machines including 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis types with workers inspecting them Before picking a machine, it helps to understand how different setups handle real jobs. Not all routers are built for the same type of work, and the difference shows up fast once you move past hobby projects and into production. This is where routing machining becomes less about “can it cut?” and more about “can it cut accurately, all day, without babysitting?” Machine Type What It Does Best Where It's Commonly Used 3-Axis Routers Flat cutting, pockets, slots, simple 2.5D carving Sign shops, cabinetry, panel cutting, nested-based furniture 4-Axis Routers Adds rotary cutting for cylindrical or wrapped features Decorative columns, round signs, curved trims 5-Axis Routers Multi-angle cutting without repositioning the part Complex molds, sculpted surfaces, aerospace-style geometry Desktop Machines Small, low-power, limited materials DIY projects, prototyping, small workshops Industrial Machines Large beds, high power, full production workloads Factories, high-volume routing lines, commercial shops A professional routing cnc machine focuses on rigidity and repeatability. That matters more than flashy features. When shops talk about upgrading their routing cnc machine, they're usually chasing better accuracy over long production runs and tighter control over vibration during routing machining tasks. 3-Axis Routers These are the workhorses. Most shops start here. A 3-axis router moves along X, Y, and Z and handles the bulk of flat cutting tasks. If you're making cabinet sheets, signs, or structural panels, this setup does the job without drama. 4-Axis & 5-Axis Routers Once parts need angled cuts, undercuts, or sculpted surfaces, extra axes matter. A 4-axis router adds rotation, while a 5-axis machine brings full freedom of movement. This pushes routing machining into more advanced territory, where precision and tool orientation become just as important as cutting speed. Desktop vs Industrial Machines Desktop routers are entry-level tools. They're lighter, smaller, and designed for lower cutting forces. An industrial routing cnc machine , on the other hand, is built for long shifts, thick stock, higher spindle loads, and consistent output. Materials for the CNC Routing Process (Istock) Your material choice controls almost everything: cut quality, tool wear, and final edge finish. Even the best routing cnc machine will struggle if the feeds, speeds, and tooling don't match the material properly. Wood & MDF Wood and MDF (Medium Density Fiberboard) , these are the two easiest materials you'll run on a CNC router. They cut cleanly, you can crank the speeds up, and your tool wear stays low (because it's just wood and MDF!). This makes them ideal for work with high-volume like decorative panels or cabinetry. MDF specifically gives you those super smooth edges, but you'd better have good dust extraction ready; MDF produces a large amount of fine dust. Acrylic & Plastics Plastics cut cleanly with a sharp tool and controlled heat. Acrylic needs careful chip evacuation and polished tooling to avoid melting or edge haze. This is where stable spindle speed and smart feed rates matter most in CNC routing setups. Composite Materials Aluminum composite panels, PVC foam boards, and fiberglass-reinforced sheets and other similar materials sit in the middle of it all. They're tougher than pure plastics but not as aggressive as metals, unlike both of these extremes. A well-tuned routing cnc machine handles composites easily when vibration is controlled and chip removal is consistent. Soft Metals Aluminum and thin brass can be routed, but only with conservative cutting parameters because these metals generate heat quickly, amplify vibration on lighter machines, and wear down router bits much faster than wood or plastics. This is where lighter machines fall short and true industrial CNC routing systems show their value through stability, torque, and tool life. People confuse routing and milling all the time. On the surface, they look similar: spinning tool, moving table, material getting cut. But the machines are built for completely different jobs, and that difference becomes clear the moment you start running parts. CNC Routing vs. Milling: Key Differences You Should Know Key Differences in Machine Structure Routers are typically lighter, with wide gantries designed for large sheet materials. Mills are heavier, more compact, and built to resist high cutting forces in metals. The cnc routing process prioritizes speed and surface coverage, while milling favors stiffness and torque. Cutting Tools and Spindle Speed Comparison Routers spin fast, often 12,000–24,000 RPM, with long, slender tools ideal for wood and plastics. Mills run slower but with far more torque. This is where the cnc routing process shines for fast chip evacuation and clean edges, compared to milling's slower, heavy metal removal. Watch a router in action and you'll see the toolpath zip across the material, while a mill moves more deliberately. Knowing how to optimize your toolpaths can save hours of work. Learn more about effective strategies in our Comprehensive Guide to CNC Toolpath . Material Compatibility: Wood, Plastic, Metal Routing excels at wood, MDF, foam, acrylic, and composites. Milling dominates steels and harder metals. Routers can handle soft aluminum, but that's about their limit. However, for extremely hard metals or ultra-precise shapes that even milling cannot achieve reliably, wire EDM becomes the preferred option . Wire EDM removes material with minimal mechanical force, maintaining tight tolerances and intricate geometries. Check out our guide on How EDM Wire Cutting Works to learn when and why this method outperforms routing. Precision, Tolerance, and Surface Finish Mills win on tight tolerances, routers win on speed and large-format work. The cnc routing process typically delivers ±0.1–0.3 mm tolerances depending on machine rigidity, tooling, and material. For wood-based materials, however, be aware that changes in humidity can cause expansion or contraction, meaning the router's effective precision also depends on the stability of the material itself. JLCCNC may not offer CNC routing yet, but if you're after precise, high-quality parts with tight tolerances, our CNC milling services have you covered . With years of experience and per-part costs starting at just $5, we handle metals, plastics, and composites with professional-grade accuracy. Upload your design and get an instant quote today. How Do I Start CNC Routing? Starting out isn't about buying the fanciest machine. It's about understanding the workflow so you don't waste material and time. Choose the Right CNC Router and Tools Pick a machine that matches your material and part size. Too small, and you'll fight it constantly. Too light, and vibration kills edge quality. Understanding the cnc routing process early helps avoid equipment regret later. Learn Basic CAD/CAM Software You don't need to be a designer. You need to know how to generate clean toolpaths. Once you understand, CAM stops feeling like guesswork and starts feeling logical. Run Test Cuts and Adjust Cutting Parameters Never trust the first cut. Test, measure, adjust. Feed rate, spindle speed, depth of cut, these are the levers that control quality. Applications of CNC Routing (Istock) Sign Making Acrylic letters, PVC boards, aluminum composite panels, this is classic cnc routing territory. Clean edges and fast turnaround are the big wins. Furniture & Panel Cutting Nested-based manufacturing relies heavily on cnc routing for cabinet parts, shelves, and structural panels. High speed and repeatability make it perfect for production runs. Prototyping Quick turnarounds, fast revisions, and low material waste make routing ideal for early product development, especially with plastics and wood-based sheets. The Real Reasons CNC Routing Dominates CNC routing isn't just a complicated way to move a cutter; it completely transforms your productivity and precision output. You need to understand why routing keeps crushing manual methods and even specialized machines. Unwavering Accuracy, No Drift Allowed Once the final toolpath is programmed, that cut is locked in. Every single pass is identical. We're talking zero drift. This means your workflow runs cleaner, you stop wasting expensive material on mistakes, and your final product stack is perfectly uniform. Try cutting fifty identical cabinet doors manually. The last door will inevitably be slightly off due to operator fatigue. A CNC routing machine produces the 50th door exactly like the first. Speed That Changes Your Bottom Line Routers are incredibly efficient at clearing material fast. High spindle speeds combined with optimized feed rates mean you can literally remove large volumes of material efficiently without sacrificing quality. For things like cutting entire stacks of MDF or complex acrylic signage, that speed doesn't just look good, it means dramatically more output per shift . Versus Lasers: A laser might be precise, but it can be excruciatingly slow cutting thick wood. A router bit chews right through that material quickly, saving hours on bulk jobs. Handling the Big Stuff Unlike traditional milling machines, which are often confined to small, heavy blocks of metal, routing machines easily handle oversized panels and sheets. This is the only practical way to process large formats for cabinetry, custom architectural signage, or furniture components. One Machine, Dozens of Materials You don't actually need a separate specialized machine for every job that walks in the door. CNC routing handles nearly everything: wood, MDF, foam, plastics, composites, and even lighter metals . That same router, just by changing the bit and adjusting the settings, can instantly swap from running acrylic displays to cutting aluminum paneling. It makes job scheduling way simpler, plus it cuts down significantly on how much expensive equipment you have to buy. FAQ Q: What materials can a CNC router cut? A: Wood, MDF, acrylic, plastics, soft metals, and composites. Some high-end routers can also handle aluminum or brass, but they are better at fast cutting of lightweight or sheet materials. Q: How precise is CNC routing? A: Typical tolerance ranges from ±0.1mm to ±0.3mm, depending on machine rigidity, material, and tool choice. Repeatability is one of its strongest advantages. Q: Can a CNC router replace a milling machine? A: Not entirely. Routers are made for speed and large-format cutting, especially in wood or plastics. Milling machines handle harder metals and require tighter tolerances. Q: Do I need CAD/CAM software? A: Yes. Toolpaths, nesting, and cutting strategies are all generated in CAM software. CAD helps you design the part, but CAM turns it into a cut-ready program. Q: What maintenance does a CNC router need? A: Keep rails clean, check belt tension, lubricate bearings, and ensure spindle cooling if applicable. Routine checks keep accuracy high and downtime low. Understanding what is CNC routing clarifies why it's the dominant method for things like cabinetry and sign-making. You see CNC routing everywhere in actual production shops: Furniture panels and cabinet doors. Custom engraved lettering and large signs. Acrylic point-of-sale displays. Foam inserts for packaging. Light sheet components made of aluminum. Any time you need clean, repeatable cuts on sheet material, routing is almost always the fastest, most cost-effective method available. How CNC Routing Works CNC routing works by following a precise, computer-generated toolpath to remove material from a workpiece. The process starts with a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) file , which defines the shape, dimensions, and features of the part. This CAD design is then imported into CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing) software , where toolpaths, cutting speeds, spindle speeds, and depths of cut are calculated. Once the program is ready, it is sent to the CNC router. The router uses servo-controlled motors to move the cutting tool along multiple axes—typically X, Y, and Z for standard 3-axis machines, with additional rotary axes for more complex 4- or 5-axis setups. The spinning router bit removes material according to the programmed path, producing precise cuts, grooves, and contours without the need for manual intervention. Key steps in the CNC routing process include: Material Setup – Secure the workpiece on the router bed using clamps or vacuum tables to prevent movement during cutting. Tool Selection – Choose the appropriate router bit for the material and type of cut, considering diameter, flute type, and coating. Spindle and Feed Settings – Adjust spindle speed, feed rate, and depth per pass based on material type, thickness, and bit geometry. Test Cuts – Run a small test cut to verify toolpath accuracy, edge quality, and material behavior before full production. Full Production Run – Execute the complete toolpath with continuous monitoring of material removal, chip evacuation, and machine stability. CNC routing allows for high repeatability, consistent surface finish, and complex geometries across a wide range of materials. Unlike manual routing, it eliminates human error, fatigue, and variability, making it ideal for large-format panels, decorative elements, signage, and prototyping . By understanding how CNC routing works, operators can optimize toolpaths, reduce cycle times, extend tool life, and achieve high-quality results with minimal material waste. Types of CNC Routing Machines Multiple CNC routing machines including 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis types with workers inspecting them Before picking a machine, it helps to understand how different setups handle real jobs. Not all routers are built for the same type of work, and the difference shows up fast once you move past hobby projects and into production. This is where routing machining becomes less about “can it cut?” and more about “can it cut accurately, all day, without babysitting?” Machine Type What It Does Best Where It's Commonly Used 3-Axis Routers Flat cutting, pockets, slots, simple 2.5D carving Sign shops, cabinetry, panel cutting, nested-based furniture 4-Axis Routers Adds rotary cutting for cylindrical or wrapped features Decorative columns, round signs, curved trims 5-Axis Routers Multi-angle cutting without repositioning the part Complex molds, sculpted surfaces, aerospace-style geometry Desktop Machines Small, low-power, limited materials DIY projects, prototyping, small workshops Industrial Machines Large beds, high power, full production workloads Factories, high-volume routing lines, commercial shops A professional routing cnc machine focuses on rigidity and repeatability. That matters more than flashy features. When shops talk about upgrading their routing cnc machine, they're usually chasing better accuracy over long production runs and tighter control over vibration during routing machining tasks. 3-Axis Routers These are the workhorses. Most shops start here. A 3-axis router moves along X, Y, and Z and handles the bulk of flat cutting tasks. If you're making cabinet sheets, signs, or structural panels, this setup does the job without drama. 4-Axis & 5-Axis Routers Once parts need angled cuts, undercuts, or sculpted surfaces, extra axes matter. A 4-axis router adds rotation, while a 5-axis machine brings full freedom of movement. This pushes routing machining into more advanced territory, where precision and tool orientation become just as important as cutting speed. Desktop vs Industrial Machines Desktop routers are entry-level tools. They're lighter, smaller, and designed for lower cutting forces. An industrial routing cnc machine , on the other hand, is built for long shifts, thick stock, higher spindle loads, and consistent output. Materials for the CNC Routing Process (Istock) Your material choice controls almost everything: cut quality, tool wear, and final edge finish. Even the best routing cnc machine will struggle if the feeds, speeds, and tooling don't match the material properly. Wood & MDF Wood and MDF (Medium Density Fiberboard) , these are the two easiest materials you'll run on a CNC router. They cut cleanly, you can crank the speeds up, and your tool wear stays low (because it's just wood and MDF!). This makes them ideal for work with high-volume like decorative panels or cabinetry. MDF specifically gives you those super smooth edges, but you'd better have good dust extraction ready; MDF produces a large amount of fine dust. Acrylic & Plastics Plastics cut cleanly with a sharp tool and controlled heat. Acrylic needs careful chip evacuation and polished tooling to avoid melting or edge haze. This is where stable spindle speed and smart feed rates matter most in CNC routing setups. Composite Materials Aluminum composite panels, PVC foam boards, and fiberglass-reinforced sheets and other similar materials sit in the middle of it all. They're tougher than pure plastics but not as aggressive as metals, unlike both of these extremes. A well-tuned routing cnc machine handles composites easily when vibration is controlled and chip removal is consistent. Soft Metals Aluminum and thin brass can be routed, but only with conservative cutting parameters because these metals generate heat quickly, amplify vibration on lighter machines, and wear down router bits much faster than wood or plastics. This is where lighter machines fall short and true industrial CNC routing systems show their value through stability, torque, and tool life. People confuse routing and milling all the time. On the surface, they look similar: spinning tool, moving table, material getting cut. But the machines are built for completely different jobs, and that difference becomes clear the moment you start running parts. CNC Routing vs. Milling: Key Differences You Should Know Key Differences in Machine Structure Routers are typically lighter, with wide gantries designed for large sheet materials. Mills are heavier, more compact, and built to resist high cutting forces in metals. The cnc routing process prioritizes speed and surface coverage, while milling favors stiffness and torque. Cutting Tools and Spindle Speed Comparison Routers spin fast, often 12,000–24,000 RPM, with long, slender tools ideal for wood and plastics. Mills run slower but with far more torque. This is where the cnc routing process shines for fast chip evacuation and clean edges, compared to milling's slower, heavy metal removal. Watch a router in action and you'll see the toolpath zip across the material, while a mill moves more deliberately. Knowing how to optimize your toolpaths can save hours of work. Learn more about effective strategies in our Comprehensive Guide to CNC Toolpath . Material Compatibility: Wood, Plastic, Metal Routing excels at wood, MDF, foam, acrylic, and composites. Milling dominates steels and harder metals. Routers can handle soft aluminum, but that's about their limit. However, for extremely hard metals or ultra-precise shapes that even milling cannot achieve reliably, wire EDM becomes the preferred option . Wire EDM removes material with minimal mechanical force, maintaining tight tolerances and intricate geometries. Check out our guide on How EDM Wire Cutting Works to learn when and why this method outperforms routing. Precision, Tolerance, and Surface Finish Mills win on tight tolerances, routers win on speed and large-format work. The cnc routing process typically delivers ±0.1–0.3 mm tolerances depending on machine rigidity, tooling, and material. For wood-based materials, however, be aware that changes in humidity can cause expansion or contraction, meaning the router's effective precision also depends on the stability of the material itself. JLCCNC may not offer CNC routing yet, but if you're after precise, high-quality parts with tight tolerances, our CNC milling services have you covered . With years of experience and per-part costs starting at just $5, we handle metals, plastics, and composites with professional-grade accuracy. Upload your design and get an instant quote today. How Do I Start CNC Routing? Starting out isn't about buying the fanciest machine. It's about understanding the workflow so you don't waste material and time. Choose the Right CNC Router and Tools Pick a machine that matches your material and part size. Too small, and you'll fight it constantly. Too light, and vibration kills edge quality. Understanding the cnc routing process early helps avoid equipment regret later. Learn Basic CAD/CAM Software You don't need to be a designer. You need to know how to generate clean toolpaths. Once you understand, CAM stops feeling like guesswork and starts feeling logical. Run Test Cuts and Adjust Cutting Parameters Never trust the first cut. Test, measure, adjust. Feed rate, spindle speed, depth of cut, these are the levers that control quality. Applications of CNC Routing (Istock) Sign Making Acrylic letters, PVC boards, aluminum composite panels, this is classic cnc routing territory. Clean edges and fast turnaround are the big wins. Furniture & Panel Cutting Nested-based manufacturing relies heavily on cnc routing for cabinet parts, shelves, and structural panels. High speed and repeatability make it perfect for production runs. Prototyping Quick turnarounds, fast revisions, and low material waste make routing ideal for early product development, especially with plastics and wood-based sheets. The Real Reasons CNC Routing Dominates CNC routing isn't just a complicated way to move a cutter; it completely transforms your productivity and precision output. You need to understand why routing keeps crushing manual methods and even specialized machines. Unwavering Accuracy, No Drift Allowed Once the final toolpath is programmed, that cut is locked in. Every single pass is identical. We're talking zero drift. This means your workflow runs cleaner, you stop wasting expensive material on mistakes, and your final product stack is perfectly uniform. Try cutting fifty identical cabinet doors manually. The last door will inevitably be slightly off due to operator fatigue. A CNC routing machine produces the 50th door exactly like the first. Speed That Changes Your Bottom Line Routers are incredibly efficient at clearing material fast. High spindle speeds combined with optimized feed rates mean you can literally remove large volumes of material efficiently without sacrificing quality. For things like cutting entire stacks of MDF or complex acrylic signage, that speed doesn't just look good, it means dramatically more output per shift . Versus Lasers: A laser might be precise, but it can be excruciatingly slow cutting thick wood. A router bit chews right through that material quickly, saving hours on bulk jobs. Handling the Big Stuff Unlike traditional milling machines, which are often confined to small, heavy blocks of metal, routing machines easily handle oversized panels and sheets. This is the only practical way to process large formats for cabinetry, custom architectural signage, or furniture components. One Machine, Dozens of Materials You don't actually need a separate specialized machine for every job that walks in the door. CNC routing handles nearly everything: wood, MDF, foam, plastics, composites, and even lighter metals . That same router, just by changing the bit and adjusting the settings, can instantly swap from running acrylic displays to cutting aluminum paneling. It makes job scheduling way simpler, plus it cuts down significantly on how much expensive equipment you have to buy. FAQ Q: What materials can a CNC router cut? A: Wood, MDF, acrylic, plastics, soft metals, and composites. Some high-end routers can also handle aluminum or brass, but they are better at fast cutting of lightweight or sheet materials. Q: How precise is CNC routing? A: Typical tolerance ranges from ±0.1mm to ±0.3mm, depending on machine rigidity, material, and tool choice. Repeatability is one of its strongest advantages. Q: Can a CNC router replace a milling machine? A: Not entirely. Routers are made for speed and large-format cutting, especially in wood or plastics. Milling machines handle harder metals and require tighter tolerances. Q: Do I need CAD/CAM software? A: Yes. Toolpaths, nesting, and cutting strategies are all generated in CAM software. CAD helps you design the part, but CAM turns it into a cut-ready program. Q: What maintenance does a CNC router need? A: Keep rails clean, check belt tension, lubricate bearings, and ensure spindle cooling if applicable. Routine checks keep accuracy high and downtime low. PCBWay's 3D & CNC services always well received by our customers. Now we have an in-depth cooperation with FreeCAD. FreeCAD is an open-source parametric 3D modeler made primarily to design real-life objects of any size. It is widely used among engineers. Now when you complete the 3D design on FreeCAD, you can place an order on PCBWay with just one click. FreeCAD will pass step files to us. You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files (usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before production. Installation from the official FreeCAD tools Just click the "tools" ----“Addon manager”---Choose the "PCBWay” from the selection list, click and install it. Manual installation You can also download the latest file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-FreeCAD , then click the "Macro", put the python file in the path, and click the “execute“ As a sponsor of FreeCAD, we will always support its development. Verify Now Blog > Stage 1: Frequency-Controlled Atomic-State Demonstrator Stage 1: Frequency-Controlled Atomic-State Demonstrator by: Engineer Aug 07,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in Engineering Technical Atomic Physics Spectroscopy Frequency Control Electronics Research Summary： This first-stage prototype uses a controlled RF, microwave, or optical source to change and measure a known atomic or molecular state. It validates the established relationship hf = ΔE while logging frequency, field strength, pulse duration, polarization, sample conditions, detector response, and safety interlocks. It does not claim to create a new element. Stage 1 establishes the part of the concept that is already supported by atomic physics: an electromagnetic field can drive a transition when photon energy matches an allowed energy difference, hf = ΔE. System flow: 1. Isolated DC power bus. 2. Frequency and waveform controller. 3. Low-power RF, microwave, or optical source. 4. Known atomic or molecular sample. 5. Spectrometer, photodetector, or spin-response detector. 6. Computer control and evidence log. The experiment records actual frequency and linewidth, field amplitude or optical power, pulse duration, phase, polarization, sample composition, temperature, detector calibration, and background runs. The feedback controller changes the source settings and compares the measured response with the predicted resonance. Gate 1 passes only when the expected absorption, fluorescence, ionization, or spin response occurs near the predicted transition and disappears in beam-off or off-frequency controls. Verify Now Blog > Stage 2: Reaction Feasibility and Energy-Control Simulator Stage 2: Reaction Feasibility and Energy-Control Simulator by: Engineer Aug 07,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in Engineering Technical Simulation Nuclear Physics Isotopes Scientific Computing Energy Summary： Stage 2 is a software-first feasibility system for a chosen isotope. It combines periodic-table and isotope data, target selection, projectile energy, conservation laws, reaction thresholds, cross-sections, expected detector counts, energy balance, uncertainty, and safety requirements. It produces a preregistered experiment proposal rather than operating high-energy hardware. Stage 2 converts a desired isotope into a complete testable reaction proposal before any high-energy equipment is considered. Inputs include the desired element and isotope, candidate target or feedstock, projectile type, energy spectrum, flux, geometry, exposure time, and detector configuration. The simulator first checks energy, momentum, charge, angular momentum, and relevant particle accounting. A reaction that fails a conservation test is rejected. For an allowed reaction, the expected detected events are estimated from: N_detected = luminosity × cross-section × time × detector efficiency. The model also calculates competing reaction channels, background counts, uncertainty, thermal load, activation risk, cooling demand, shielding class, total operating power, recoverable energy, and net external power. Required modules: - Periodic-table and isotope database. - Reaction-network engine. - Conservation-law checker. - Threshold and cross-section model. - Detector and background model. - Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. - Energy and safety ledger. - Versioned evidence record. Gate 2 passes only when the proposal contains a balanced reaction, defensible cross-section, detectable predicted yield, complete detector signatures, control runs, and a qualified-facility safety plan. The deliverable is a preregistered experiment package stating what outcome confirms the hypothesis and what outcome rejects or constrains it. Verify Now Blog > Congratulations on the Successful Development of PCBWay's 24-Layer, 6-Order Arbitrary Interconnection HDI PCB Congratulations on the Successful Development of PCBWay's 24-Layer, 6-Order Arbitrary Interconnection HDI PCB by: Mia Nov 04,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in HDI PCB HDI PCB Interposer PCB With the continuous development of the integrated circuit industry, the connections between chips have become increasingly complex. Traditional PCB technology faces limitations in applications with higher frequency and speed requirements. Achieving stable and reliable connections between high-speed and high-density chips has become critically important. Moreover, as the power consumption of chips continues to rise, heat generation has also increased, necessitating an effective cooling system to maintain normal chip operation. As a result, the interposer PCB, a new type of PCB, has emerged. The so-called interposer PCB is a highly precise, high-layer arbitrary interconnection HDI PCB. It serves as a critical component for connecting and integrating different electronic components and acts as an intermediary layer for chip connections. It achieves electrical connections through pad leads and interconnects with the chip’s micro bumps (uBump) and the routing in the intermediary layer. The intermediary layer utilizes through-silicon vias (TSV) to connect upper and lower layers. The design characteristics of this PCB include inner layers connected to the outer layers through laser microvias and dense routing, resulting in a multi-structure with BGA connections on the top side and pad connections on the bottom side. Interposer PCBs hold exceptional value and significance in improving various performance aspects of integrated circuits. First, interposer PCBs can provide higher connection speeds and reliability for semiconductor products. Made from high-performance materials, interposer PCBs enable short-distance, high-density connections between integrated circuits, significantly increasing chip data transmission rates. Second, interposer PCB technology addresses signal integrity and power consumption issues. By utilizing interposer technology, signal pins can be directly connected to the interposer layer, reducing the length of signal transmission paths, thereby minimizing signal loss and enhancing signal integrity. Third, the interposer layer also serves a thermal management role, effectively reducing chip temperatures. Finally, interposer PCB technology facilitates the connection between heterogeneous integrated circuits. By placing integrated circuits with different functions on the same interposer layer, it enables interconnections between various chips, thereby enhancing the overall performance and efficiency of semiconductor products. In conclusion, interposer PCBs are widely used in fields such as high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, data centers, and communications. In high-performance computing systems, interposer technology can connect multiple processing chips, enabling larger-scale computing capabilities. In the field of artificial intelligence, interposer technology facilitates interconnections between different chips, enhancing the training and inference speeds of neural networks. In data center and communication applications, interposer technology provides higher transmission rates and bandwidth to meet the demands of big data processing and high-speed communication. As a leading manufacturer of high-end HDI PCBs, PCBWay keeps pace with market trends. In response to the urgent demand from clients for high-order arbitrary interconnection (Anylayer) HDI boards, our product research institute has dedicated itself to overcoming technical challenges, ultimately achieving the successful development of high-layer, high-order arbitrary interconnection interposer PCBs. Here, we will showcase the details of this high-precision circuit product using the 24-layer, 6-order Anylayer HDI PCB as an example. 1. Product Parameters 2. Product Structure 3. Technical Challenges Challenge 1: The buried via PCB thickness from L7 to L18 is 1.0 mm, with a mechanical through-hole diameter of 0.1 mm, resulting in a hole aspect ratio of 10:1, making mechanical drilling difficult. Challenge 2: The BGA pitch is 0.35 mm, and the distance from the hole to the conductor trace is 0.13 mm, which makes it easy for misalignment during multiple laminations. Challenge 3: The trace width/spacing is 2.4/3 mil, and it features dense routing. Below are some routing diagrams. 4. Be Part of the PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest! by: PCBWay Sep 03,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News We are glad to announce that PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest has arrived. Prior to this, PCBWay successfully held six design contests. In each contest, we saw many eye-catching projects shared by outstanding and creative electronic engineers and enthusiasts. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest will continue the previous purpose, which is to encourage more and more people to explore the charm of electronic design and participate in it. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . In this contest, in addition to the two themes of Electronic Project and Mechanical Project that have appeared before, we also introduced STM32 Project, hoping to give designers more room to perform. The contest will start on September 2nd, 2024, and project submissions will be accepted until January 19th, 2025. After this, the judging phase will begin, and the final winners will be announced on the PCBWay Blog on March 10th, 2025. Two ways to participate in the contest: Go to the contest page, find the Participate Now button and click it. In this case, the submitted project will automatically be entered into the competition; participants only need to select the theme of entry. Please note that if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. After filling in all the project information, simply click "Submit" at the bottom of the page. Go to the SharedProject Community ( https://www.pcbway.com/project/shareproject/ ) and click Create a project. Select the theme you are going to participate in. Similarly, if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. Hint: Sharing complete project files, including Gerber, BOM, Centroid file, schematics, 3D files, and so on will increase the chances of receiving a higher score. Awards and corresponding prizes: The First Prize : 1 winner, $1500 Cash + $200 Coupon + A Palm-sized Robot Dog*1 The Second Prize : 2 winners, $1000 Cash + $100 Coupon + Raspberry Pi 5 4GB *1 The Third Prize : 3 winners, $500 Cash + $50 Coupon + OpenMV4 H7 R2 Cam Smart Camera *1 Popular Design Prize : 10 winners, $100 Cash + $20 Coupon + $10 3D Printing Coupon + Multimeter ZTY890DPro *1 Participation Prize : Raspberry Pi Pico * 1 STM32 Great Project Prize : Six-Claw Multifunctional Aluminum Alloy Soldering Table *1 For more detailed information about the contest, please refer to: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . If there are any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment below.We wish you the best of luck and look forward to your innovative designs! Verify Now Blog > Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay by: PCBWay May 30,2025 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News PCBWay recognizes the significant role it plays within the supply chain and broader society, along with the potential impact of its operations. To this end, we have established and strictly enforce the following principles, which not only govern our own conduct but also set clear expectations for our partners. Our goal is to ensure full legal and regulatory compliance, promote long-term sustainability, and generate a positive impact on society. Human Rights and Labor Protection No employment of individuals below the legal working age; all forms of forced or bonded labor are strictly prohibited. Discrimination and harassment in the workplace are not tolerated; an inclusive work environment for persons with disabilities is encouraged. Employees must be provided with fair compensation and reasonable rest periods, and their rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining must be respected. Business Ethics and Compliance Offering, promising, soliciting, or accepting any form of bribery is strictly prohibited; effective conflict of interest management and whistleblowing mechanisms must be in place. All financial and business records must accurately, completely, and truthfully reflect the underlying transactions. Full compliance with international sanctions, export controls, and other applicable laws and regulations is required. Supply Chain Responsibility and Sustainable Procurement PCBWay and its partners are required to extend the principles outlined in this document to all levels of entities within the supply chain. Priority should be given to selecting partners that are legally compliant, socially responsible, and committed to sustainable development. Identify social, labor, and environmental risks related to operations, and develop corresponding control and mitigation measures. Encourage partners to prioritize local sourcing to support regional economic development and job creation. Environmental Protection and Workplace Safety Actively implement environmental protection measures and continuously promote energy conservation and emission reduction; Ensure that all waste and hazardous materials are disposed of in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. The procurement or use of prohibited materials is not allowed. Provide employees with a safe working environment and health support mechanisms to prevent occupational injuries and health risks. PCBWay has fully adopted the DHL GoGreen transportation service in 2025 to reduce carbon emissions in the supply chain and promote the development of a green supply chain, with an initial target of reducing emissions by 30%. Information Protection and Transparent Governance Establish a comprehensive security system to strictly protect the confidentiality of customer data, drawings, and other business information. Comply with relevant laws and regulations to safeguard the personal data of customers and employees. Ensure that financial records are true, accurate, and complete, and prohibit any illegal activities. PCBWay will ensure the implementation of the above principles in actual cooperation and reserves the right to take action against any violations. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. It’s Trickier Than You Think. But because of an ever-changing patchwork of trade rules, not every product will be charged an astronomical tariff, trade lawyers, customs brokers and importers say. In some cases, tariffs will pile on other tariffs. In other instances, they can reduce costs, while other times they can cancel out new ones. The new 125 percent rate that President Trump imposed will in many cases be added on top of long-existing duties. There are four main categories of tariffs that are imposed on goods from China. Note: The tariff on auto parts comes into effect in early May. The average provided for the base rate is calculated by the World Trade Organization, which computes an average of all tariff lines. A large share of U.S. imports are assigned a 0% duty, but there are some very high rates in the tariff schedule. For further inquiries, please contact: logistics@pcbway.com Update on May 12th The Government of the United States of America (the “United States”) and the Government of the People’s Republic of China (“China”), Recognizing the importance of their bilateral economic and trade relationship to both countries and the global economy; Recognizing the importance of a sustainable, long-term, and mutually beneficial economic and trade relationship; Reflecting on their recent discussions and believing that continued discussions have the potential to address the concerns of each side in their economic and trade relationship; and Moving forward in the spirit of mutual opening, continued communication, cooperation, and mutual respect; The Parties commit to take the following actions by May 14, 2025 : The United States will (i) modify the application of the additional ad valorem rate of duty on articles of China (including articles of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macau Special Administrative Region) set forth in Executive Order 14257 of April 2, 2025, by suspending 24 percentage points of that rate for an initial period of 90 days, while retaining the remaining ad valorem rate of 10 percent on those articles pursuant to the terms of said Order; and (ii) removing the modified additional ad valorem rates of duty on those articles imposed by Executive Order 14259 of April 8, 2025 and Executive Order 14266 of April 9, 2025. China will (i) modify accordingly the application of the additional ad valorem rate of duty on articles of the United States set forth in Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 4 of 2025, by suspending 24 percentage points of that rate for an initial period of 90 days, while retaining the remaining additional ad valorem rate of 10 percent on those articles, and removing the modified additional ad valorem rates of duty on those articles imposed by Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 5 of 2025 and Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 6 of 2025; and (ii) adopt all necessary administrative measures to suspend or remove the non-tariff countermeasures taken against the United States since April 2, 2025. After taking the aforementioned actions, the Parties will establish a mechanism to continue discussions about economic and trade relations. The representative from the Chinese side for these discussions will be He Lifeng, Vice Premier of the State Council, and the representatives from the U.S. side will be Scott Bessent, Secretary of the Treasury, and Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative. These discussions may be conducted alternately in China and the United States, or a third country upon agreement of the Parties. As required, the two sides may conduct working-level consultations on relevant economic and trade issues. https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/05/joint-statement-on-u-s-china-economic-and-trade-meeting-in-geneva/ Updated on April 25th **Presidential Executive Order on Tariff Adjustments for Chinese Goods** On April 8, 2025 (local time), U.S. President Donald Trump issued an executive order announcing the following tariff measures on goods originating from China (including Hong Kong, China): 1. **Elimination of De Minimis Exemption for Chinese-origin Goods** 2. **Additional 125%+20% (If it is the category under 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, the tariff exemption is 125%) Tariff on High-value Chinese Goods** 3.Fedex Official: For B2C shipments, a valid FedEx account number is required. 4.If the product falls under HTS categories 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 125% tariff exemption. However, DHL’s customs declaration system may inaccurately apply or fail to recognize the 125% exemption. If the recipient finds that the product is indeed eligible for the exemption but the 125% duty relief was not applied, they must file a dispute with DHL immediately, as there is a strict deadline for appeals. By the time the sender notices the issue, the appeal window may have already closed. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. The exemption scope of 9903.01.32 includes semiconductors, as well as some goods listed by the United States within the HS list. The applicable exemption scope of 9903.01.33 includes automobiles and some parts and components, and it is related to the Section 232 list. 9903.01.63 refers to goods other than those within the scopes of 9903.01.32 and 9903.01.33, and an additional 125% tariff will be imposed on them. =============================================================================================================================================== How Much Are Tariffs on Chinese Goods? It’s Trickier Than You Think. But because of an ever-changing patchwork of trade rules, not every product will be charged an astronomical tariff, trade lawyers, customs brokers and importers say. In some cases, tariffs will pile on other tariffs. In other instances, they can reduce costs, while other times they can cancel out new ones. The new 125 percent rate that President Trump imposed will in many cases be added on top of long-existing duties. There are four main categories of tariffs that are imposed on goods from China. Note: The tariff on auto parts comes into effect in early May. The average provided for the base rate is calculated by the World Trade Organization, which computes an average of all tariff lines. A large share of U.S. imports are assigned a 0% duty, but there are some very high rates in the tariff schedule. Rates ultimately depend on what is imported, what materials are used (from where), which special rates are applied and what sorts of products are exempt. New tariff rates on select goods from China Note: Rates are rounded to the nearest whole number.
